 agenda item being considered, the public hearing or non-public hearing agenda item will automatically be
 continued to the next regularly scheduled City Council meeting. If you will require special accommodations, due

 Manchester Boulevard, First Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301. All requests for special
 accommodations must be received 72 hours prior to the day of the Council Meetings.

Inglewood, California
  September 24, 2019

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on
  Tuesday, September 24, 2019, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called
  the City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing
  Authority, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.
  The City Clerk/ Successor Agency Secretary/ Housing Authority Secretary
  announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority  Chairman  Butts,  Council
  Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members Dotson, Morales and
  Franklin; and
  Absent:  Council  Member/Successor  Agency
  Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
  follows:
  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Asst. City Manager/CFO
  Aisha Thompson  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons
  present who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing
  Authority on any item on the Agenda.

  There was no response.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded
  by Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member
  Dotson that the demands presented to the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority dated September 19, 2019, in the amount of
  $2,718,196.41, are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said
  registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority
  Members Dotson, Morales, Franklin and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority
  Member Padilla.

  132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending
  rejection of the claim filed by Barbara Usher for alleged vehicle damage pursuant
  to Government Code 913.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, seconded by Council Member
  Dotson, and carried that the above listed claims be denied.

101  AMENDMENT TWO TO AGREEMENT NO. 19-077 APPROVED –
  COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES. Staff report dated September 24, 2019, was

  1
 September 24, 2019

  presented recommending approval of Amendment Two to Agreement No. 19-077
  for Welfare-to-Work Vocational, Intermediary and Direct Services by and
  between the County of Los Angeles and the City of Inglewood serving as the
  administrative entity for the South Bay Workforce Investment Board (SBWIB).

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby approve Amendment Two to
  Agreement No. 19-077. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Padilla.

301  AMENDMENT TO AGREEMENT NO. 18-204 APPROVED – CSG
  CONSULTANTS, INC. Staff report dated September 24, 2019, was presented
  recommending approval of an amendment to Agreement No. 18-204 with CSG
  Consultants, Inc., increasing the contract by an additional $140,000 for
  professional Building Safety plan check services.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby approve an amendment to Agreement
  No. 18-204. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Padilla.

156  PAYMENT OF INVOICES SUBMITTED BY HERZOG ELECTRICAL
  AND SANTA MONICA SYSTEMS AUTHORIZED - INSTALLATION OF
  A NEW VIDEO WALL AT THE INGLEWOOD SENIOR CENTER. Staff
  report dated September 24, 2019, was presented recommending authority to pay
  invoices for the installation of a new video wall at the Inglewood Senior Center.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby authorize payments in the total amount
  of $13,461 to the following vendors: 1) Herzog Electrical in the amount of
  $3,500; and 2) Santa Monica Systems in the amount of $9,961. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Padilla.

178  PAYMENT OF INVOICE SUBMITTED BY ENTERPRISE SECURITY,
  INC., AUTHORIZED – INSTALLATION OF SEVERAL ACCESS CARD
  READERS AND OTHER ACCESS CONTROL FEATURES FOR THE
  INGLEWOOD POLICE DEPARTMENT. Staff report dated September 24,
  2019, was presented recommending authority to pay an invoice from Enterprise
  Security, Inc,, for the installation of several access card readers and other access
  control features for the Inglewood Police Department.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of
  $10,121.09. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Padilla.

178  PAYMENT OF INVOICE SUBMITTED BY MERIDIAN RAPID
  DEFENSE GROUP AUTHORIZED - BARRIER PACKAGES PROVIDED
  FOR THE TASTE OF INGLEWOOD EVENT. Staff report dated September
  24, 2019, was presented recommending authority to pay an invoice from Meridian
  Rapid Defense Group for barrier packages provided for the Taste of Inglewood
  event.

  2
 September 24, 2019

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of
  $7,661.50. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Padilla.

183  RESOLUTION NO. 19-116 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE 2018-2019
  ANNUAL CAPITAL IMPROVEMENTS PROGRAM BUDGET FOR THE
  IMPERIAL HIGHWAY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT. Staff report dated
  September 24, 2019, was presented recommending adoption of a resolution
  amending the Fiscal Year 2018-2019 Annual Capital Improvements Program
  Budget for the Imperial Highway Improvement Project.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that Resolution No. 19-116 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD AMENDING THE 2018-2019 ANNUAL BUDGET TO
  ENSURE ADEQUATE APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE CITY’S
  IMPERIAL HIGHWAY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT P610

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Padilla.

183  RESOLUTION NO. 19-117 ADOPTED – REVISING THE EFFECTIVE
  DATE FOR THE AMENDED FUNDING AGREEMENT NO. 17-274,
  BETWEEN THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD AND THE LOS ANGELES
  COUNTY METROPOLITAN AUTHORITY (MTA). Staff report dated
  September 24, 2019, was presented recommending adoption of a resolution
  revising the effective date for the Amended Funding Agreement No. 17-274,
  between the City of Inglewood and the Los Angeles County Metropolitan
  Authority (MTA).

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that Resolution No. 19-117 entitled:

  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF INGLEWOOD
  REVISING, NUNC PRO TUNC, THE EFFECTIVE DATE, FROM MAY
  8, 2018, TO MARCH 1, 2018, OF THE AMENDED AND RESTATED
  FUNDING AGREEMENT NO.: 17-274, BETWEEN THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD AND THE LOS ANGELES METROPOLITAN
  AUTHORITY

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Padilla.

183  AGREEMENT NO. 19-308  APPROVED – ENTERPRISE FLEET
  MANAGEMENT; RESOLUTION NO. 19-118 ADOPTED – AMENDING
  THE 2018-2019 FISCAL YEAR BUDGET. Staff report dated September 24,
  2019, was presented recommending approval of a four-year agreement with
  Enterprise Fleet Management to lease a total of twenty-one (21) vehicles (with the
  option to buy).

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 19-308 in
  an amount not to exceed $953,350; and 2) Adopt Resolution No. 19-118 entitled:

  3
 September 24, 2019

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA TO AUTHORIZE A BUDGET
  TRANSFER AND AMEND THE FISCAL YEAR 2018-2019 BUDGET

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Padilla.

 183  RESOLUTION NO. 19-119 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE 2018-2019
  CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM BUDGET. Staff report dated
  September 24, 2019, was presented recommending adoption of a resolution
  amending the Fiscal Year 2018-2019 Capital Improvement Program Budget by
  $306,520 for the Signal Synchronization & Timing Program for a total of
  $352,520.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that Resolution No. 19-119 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD AMENDING THE 2018-2019 ANNUAL BUDGET TO
  ENSURE ADEQUATE APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE CITY’S
  PROJECT P690

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Padilla.

131.8  PAYMENT OF INVOICES SUBMITTED BY TOT HOUSING
  SOLUTIONS AUTHORIZED - SUBSIDIZED HOUSING COSTS FOR
  SENIOR CITIZENS. Staff report dated September 24, 2019, was presented
  recommending authority to pay invoices from TOT Housing Solutions for
  subsidized housing costs for senior citizens.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount not to
  exceed $18,500. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Padilla.

142  RESOLUITON NO. 19-120 ADOPTED – ESTABLISHING THE CITY’S
  TAX-SUPPORTED APPROPRIATIONS LIMITATION FOR THE FISCAL
  YEAR 2019-2020 AS REQUIRED BY THE “GANN AMENDMENT.” Staff
  report dated September 24, 2019, was presented recommending adoption of a
  resolution establishing the City’s tax-supported appropriations limitation for
  Fiscal Year 2019-2020 as required by the “Gann Amendment.”

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales that the City Council does hereby: 1) Adopt Resolution No. 19-120
  entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD ESTABLISHING AN APPROPRIATIONS LIMIT FOR
  THE FISCAL YEAR 2019-20

  and 2) Amend the Gann Appropriation Limit for Fiscal Year 2018-2019. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and

  4
 September 24, 2019

  Absent: Council Member Padilla.

 142  RESOLUTION NO. 19-121 ADOPTED – FISCAL YEAR 2019-2020
  ANNUAL BUDGET. Staff report dated September 24, 2019, was presented
  recommending adoption of a resolution approving and adopting the Fiscal Year
  2019-2020 Annual Budget.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that Resolution No. 19-121 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING AND ADOPTING A
  BUDGET FOR FISCAL YEAR 2019-2020

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Padilla.

126  ORAL REPORTS – CITY CLERK. Yvonne Horton, City Clerk, encouraged
  everyone who is 18 years or older to register to vote. She also mentioned that
  young people, ages 16 and 17, can pre-register to vote at her office, local post
  office, or DMV. Mrs. Horton also stated that today is National Voter’s
  Registration Day, and mentioned there are light refreshments and voting literature
  in the Office of the City Clerk. Lastly, she stated that the County Registrar-
  Recorder’s Office will be conducting a Mock Election on September 28, 2019,
  and September 29, 2019, throughout the South Bay.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City
  business not elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  (Speaker Unknown), inquired if the City would consider a Lacrosse Clinic for
  kids in the community of Inglewood.

  Mr. Owen, owner of the Miracle Theater, invited everyone to attend a show
  happening Thursday, September 26, 2019, at 8:30 p.m.

  (Speaker Unknown), Vice President of the NAACP, reminded everyone of the
  Human Trafficking event happening on Saturday, September 28, 2019, at 11:00
  a.m. in Community Room A.

  Stuart Bailey commented that he attended a shredding event and is looking
  forward to the 5K run.

  Erick Holly thanked the Council Members for their support with the Police and
  Fire appreciation event. He stated that 269 people were in attendance and
  everything turned out great!

  Willie Agee commented he would like to see the ambiance around the Forum get
  better.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the
  meeting adjourned at the hour of 2:19 p.m.

  Approved this 22nd day of October, 2019

  _________________________
  Yvonne Horton, City Clerk
